pr_title: TransportListTaskAction: wait for tasks to finish asynchronously
pr_body:
Instead of synchronously blocking a thread in the management pool, add a listener on removed tasks and calls `nodeOperation` after all matched tasks have been removed. Also add a scheduled tasks to bail out after the specified wait timeout if the tasks haven't been finished.

Fixes #89564, #90988

So presumably there's an ML task that's being waited for that performs a sub-action that also runs in the `management` thread pool.

To me it seems dodgy that this code uses `sleep`: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/5f14c79320473605764840fd715ebbb31ec7491e/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/tasks/TaskManager.java#L537-L549

@nik9000 `git blame` says you originally wrote that.  Is there any reason it couldn't be rewritten to schedule checks of the task state periodically instead of blocking a thread by sleeping?  Or do @dnhatn or @DaveCTurner have any insights on this since you've done work on the task manager by the look of it?

Yikes that's definitely a bug, although we did this sort of thing a lot back in 2016 when the code was first written. Ideally we wouldn't poll at all, tasks are only unregistered in one place so we should just be able to subscribe to an event triggered from there.

review_comments: Do we need any additional tests for the new feature added in this PR or are the existing tests already indirectly testing the new feature?

I believe we worked around this by always having 2 MANAGEMENT threads in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/90193. I think we would get sufficient coverage by reverting that change, and we should do that here.
